title: add vpc control plane provisioning: multi-az interface endpoints, peering, route53
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Add full VPC control-plane provisioning for private deployments covering multi-AZ subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, cross-account peering, and Route53 private hosted zone delegation. This change extends the existing terraform modules used by the private installer so customers can opt into: 1) Multi-AZ control plane subnets with explicit AZ mappings and NAT/route propagation hooks, 2) Interface endpoints for S3, ECR, KMS and the Redwood control plane services (with security group templates and policy attachments), 3) Cross-account VPC peering helper resources and route creation for hub-spoke topologies, 4) Route53 private hosted zone delegation + conditional forwarding for shared DNS across peered accounts, 5) Upgrade hooks and idempotency guards used by the installer to perform rolling network updates with minimal disruption. Scope: terraform module changes under modules/vpc-control-plane/*; helm chart values schema updates to redwood-private-installer chart to surface endpoint toggles and DNS delegation flags; integration tests and terraform plan-validator changes; docs/installer/vpc-control-plane.md updated with example manifests and upgrade notes. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module for subnets, route tables, NAT & propagation - [x] Interface endpoint resource templates + security group rules - [x] Cross-account peering + route automation (with opt-in) - [x] Route53 delegation and conditional forwarding - [x] Helm chart values + chart schema bump - [x] Integration tests (unit tf tests + e2e plan check) - [x] Docs + upgrade notes Commits (summary): - feat(vpc): add multi-az subnet module and route propagation hooks - feat(endpoints): add interface endpoints for S3/ECR/KMS/control-plane + sg templates - feat(peering): add cross-account peering helper and route resources - chore(helm): expose endpoint/dns toggles in values.yaml and schema - test(tf): add plan-validator scenarios for peering + dns - fix(ci): terraform fmt + test fixture updates Files touched (high level): modules/vpc-control-plane/main.tf; modules/vpc-control-plane/subnets.tf; modules/vpc-control-plane/endpoints.tf; modules/vpc-control-plane/peering.tf; modules/vpc-control-plane/outputs.tf; charts/redwood-private-installer/values.yaml; charts/redwood-private-installer/templates/network-hooks.yaml; infra/tests/plan/peering-dns.scenario; docs/installer/vpc-control-plane.md; scripts/terraform/plan-validator/checks.py; examples/private/multi-az-control-plane.yaml; charts/redwood-private-installer/Chart.yaml; modules/vpc-control-plane/README.md; modules/vpc-control-plane/variables.tf Review summary: Initial review requested changes around security group least-privilege and idempotency during peering teardown; reviewer comments also asked for a stricter validation for Route53 delegation to avoid overwriting existing delegations. I addressed feedback by tightening SG rules (restricting CIDR and port ranges), adding explicit lifecycle create_before_destroy where safe, and adding a pre-flight check that errors the plan if delegation conflict is detected unless override=true is set. CI: initial run failed terraform fmt and an integration fixture mismatch; I pushed a follow-up commit (fix(ci): fmt + fixtures) and all checks passed on rerun. Merge: Squash-merged to main after approvers approved and CI green. Related tickets: ENG-4321 (control plane VPC provisioning), ENG-4350 (installer upgrade hooks). Notes for release: This is an opt-in change behind installer flags; no automatic changes for existing customers unless operator enables new values. Users performing upgrades should read docs/installer/vpc-control-plane.md for the upgrade ordering and recommended rollout windows.

review_comments: Evelyn Chen: SG rules look broad today, can we narrow ports and avoid 0.0.0.0/0 where not required?
Asha Patel: tightened SG rules in endpoints.tf, added explicit allowed_cidrs variable and updated docs to recommend using operator-managed CIDRs.
Samir Ahmed: Peering teardown could cause transient route churn during upgrades; can we add lifecycle or guards?
Asha Patel: added create_before_destroy on peering helper where feasible and a rolling upgrade hook used by the installer to reconcile routes safely.
Jordan Park: Route53 delegation needs to be safe for accounts that already manage the zone; add a pre-flight check that fails plan unless override flag is set.
Asha Patel: added pre-flight 'delegation_conflict' check in plan-validator and updated docs to show override workflow.
